main_text.p: Αὑω, Ἰύρω, Ἰύεᾳ, mergi, occidere: proprië de fole: unde Ἰύος, occidens. Anglis to dpe, mori: item to dlde, immergere se.
Αεἰϕ, madefacere, irrigare, tingere, Ἰλοπποὺς, tinctor: Angl. to dpe: fed & deto, ros, (quæ irrigatio terræ) ab eodem fonte.
Αοχεῖτη, Ἱικη, loculus, conditorium: Angl. a Dock, receptaculum navium: non portus vel statio, fed ubi subduntur & compinguntur. A Ἰοχεῖον é-tiam ducere possimus.
Ἀάκω, mordeo, Ἰάκω, animal mórsu noxium; morsus quoque, ut docet Etymologicum: Angli canem, a dogge.
Ἀιυότης, vis, acumen, dlnt: de quó suprà.
Αύπω, aquam subeo, Ἰύπης, urinator, qui aquas subit: Angli active, to dippe; & a dipper, qui alios tingit.

Ἀπυπηλίς, fructus jam adultus & maturus: jamjam (quippe ex Ἰεύς & πίπω compositum:) cafurus: Ἰπύπ & Ἰπυ-πηνς, idem, sed aliunde compofita, significant. Hinc credibile est Anglicum dyep, quod de maturis fructibus sæpe ufur-

page.notes: Greek and Hebrew-like words are set in Anglo-Saxon (black letter-like) forms; some Greek readings are approximate. Catchword/signature: "S 4" is a gathering signature at foot; "ufur-" is a catchword-like hyphenated line end. Ornamental marks in margins are not text.
